extracted.intended_audience: legal scholars, government procurement officials, DoD/Service lawyers and managers involved in Circular A-76 competitive sourcing and administrative appeals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative standards for conducting Circular A-76 competitive sourcing studies and administering the Administrative Appeal Process (AAP), including roles (IRO, SSA, AAP Authority), timeliness, scope of review, composition and qualifications of review bodies, and service-specific variations (Air Force, Army, Navy, Marine Corps).

rubrics_metrics.name: Management Plan objective
rubrics_metrics.description: The object of the Management Plan is to find “new, creative, and innovative ways” to perform the work required by the PWS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited to API 38-203 §11.3.3 and Supplemental Handbook app. I; informs how Management Plans should be evaluated for innovation in performing performance work statements (PWS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement method guidance (sealed bid vs negotiation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance regarding 'sealed bid' procedures and contracting by 'negotiation,' including rules related to 'cost/technical trade-off' methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References PAR Part 14 for sealed bids and PAR Part 15 for negotiated procurements and cost/technical trade-offs; indicates different procedural requirements depending on procurement method which affect the conduct of competitive sourcing studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Performance Plan (TPP) submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit to the Contracting Officer, and eventually the Independent Review Officer (IRO), the Technical Performance Plan (TPP) required by the solicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TPP is a required document in the solicitation process and is subject to IRO and SSA review to ensure comparability with contractor proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRO responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The IRO certifies the accuracy of the Government in-house estimate and, in negotiated procurements utilizing cost/technical trade-off principles, reviews the Government technical performance plan (TPP) to ensure it satisfies the PWS requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IRO review is a critical control point; insufficient IRO review can cause later difficulties for the SSA and raise fairness questions about the cost comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRO independence and qualification
rubrics_metrics.description: The IRO should be a qualified person from an impartial activity that is organizationally independent of the commercial activity being studied and the activity preparing the cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: API 38-203 / Supplemental Handbook require organizational independence; earlier AFI lacked detail on qualifications until an Interim Change required training for IROs and other key participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRO and participant training requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim Change to AFI 38-203 required training for IROs, as well as other key participants in the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training applies to individuals participating on the PWS team, MEO team, IRO team, Government Management Plan Team, AAP Team, etc., and is to take place prior to that component of the process; curriculum and extent were under development.

rubrics_metrics.name: SSA evaluation comparability requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The SSA must compare the MEO’s level of technical performance with that of the selected contract offer to ensure the MEO offers the same level of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the MEO level of performance is not equivalent with the selected contract offer, the SSA must direct the Government to revise the MEO level of performance (TPP/Management Plan) to achieve an 'apples-to-apples' comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the Administrative Appeal Process (AAP)
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of the AAP is to provide 'reasonable assurances' the cost comparison decision was in accordance with the procedures and requirements of Circular A-76 and the Supplemental Handbook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AAP is a procedural safeguard for stakeholders directly affected by tentative cost comparison decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible appellants / 'interested parties'
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible appellants are civilian employees and/or their union representatives 'directly affected' by a tentative cost comparison decision, as well as the competing contractor; some documents use 'interested party' more broadly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB Transmittal Memo No. 22 and service guidance emphasize that all affected parties, including the tentative winner, should review the tentative cost comparison decision and supporting documentation and may submit appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted grounds for appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals are limited to challenges specifically identifying errors on line items of the cost comparison form, instances of the agency’s denial of information, and particular incidents of agency noncompliance with the policies and procedures of Circular A-76 and AFI 38-203.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DoD Interim Guidance and service instructions reiterate this limitation; Army guidance may allow more expansive review in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: AAP non-reviewable matters / exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: The AAP does not apply to questions concerning (1) selection of one contract offeror over another, (2) the award to one contract offeror instead of another, (3) Government management decisions involving the MEO, or (4) the policies and procedures contained in Circular A-76 and the Supplemental Handbook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits the AAP to discrete procedural and costing errors rather than selection judgments or broader policy issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Former reversal-demonstration requirement rescinded
rubrics_metrics.description: Previously an appellant had to demonstrate that the challenged items would result in a reversal of the tentative cost comparison decision; this requirement was rescinded to encourage timely and comprehensive appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rescission intended to avoid conflict with prohibition on sequential administrative appeals and to ensure all relevant challenges are brought forward during initial appeal period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness — Public Review Period and filing deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: To be considered 'timely' an eligible appellant must submit their challenge in writing to the contracting officer before the end of the Public Review Period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public Review Period begins on the date all 'supporting documentation' is publicly available and ends 20 calendar days thereafter, though it can be extended to 30 calendar days for particularly complex cost comparisons with MAJCOM manpower approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: AAP Authority independence / conflict-of-interest safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: The appointed AAP Authority must be at least two organizational levels above the official that certified the MEO or independent of the activity that is the subject of the cost comparison review; Interim Change requires AAP Authority be one organizational level higher or senior in rank to the individual that served as the SSA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service guidance aims to ensure independence and to remove appearance of actual or apparent conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: AAP Review Team composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The AAP Authority appoints members of the AAP Review Team to ensure 'various experts appropriately and adequately address the appealed items.' At a minimum, the AAP Review Team must include representatives from contracting, legal, functional, manpower, and financial offices, unless the AAP Authority determines not all areas are needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to provide subject-matter expertise for fair and competent review of appealed items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirement for participants (reiterated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Installation commanders are responsible to ensure individual participants in a cost comparison receive required A-76 training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes command responsibility for participant competence; training must occur prior to participation in that process component.

rubrics_metrics.name: AAP decision timeline and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: AAP team must provide a final decision within thirty days of the end of the Public Review Period; exceptions and extensions may be granted in complex cases 'to allow proper and prudent review.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For cost comparisons expected to exceed 60 days, notification to the Air Force Manpower Office is required; timeline flexibility acknowledges complexity of large studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large-case draft findings review (300+ positions)
rubrics_metrics.description: In cost comparisons involving 300 or more positions, the AAP Review Team’s draft appeal findings are provided to 'interested parties,' who are given five working days to review and comment on the proposed findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provision allows stakeholder input on draft findings but may prolong AAP and necessitate timeline extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality of AAP decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The AAP Authority’s decision is final; the AAP does not authorize an appeal outside the agency or otherwise grant a right of judicial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service instructions and AFI 38-203 make clear administrative finality; external remedies like GAO protests may occur but AAP decisions themselves are final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Army definition of 'interested party' and broader standing
rubrics_metrics.description: DA Pamphlet 5-20 uses 'interested party' to include all 'employees of the activity under study, unions and other employee organizations representing affected federal employees, and contractors who responded to the solicitation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Army's language is broader and explicitly inclusive compared to some service instructions that used 'eligible appellant.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Army AAB expanded scope of review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Army AAB is required not only to review the issues raised in an appeal, but also 'all of the documentation supporting the in-house cost estimate and the initial decision.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives the appearance the Army seeks to identify and correct any and all errors before a final decision; broader than the Supplemental Handbook/AFI approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Army AAB timing (no extensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Army requires the AAB provide a final written decision within 30 days of receipt of the appeal, with no mention of exceptions for complex cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stricter timeline than other services; limits time for expanded reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Army appointment method and potential continuity benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: Major command (MACOM) appoints AAB members on formal orders; the AAB can sit for one specific cost-comparison or be a standing panel considering all cost comparisons during a specified period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standing panels may provide continuity and expertise in complex Circular A-76 cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Army qualifications and ineligibility for AAB membership
rubrics_metrics.description: AAB individuals must have 'some knowledge or experience in CA program requirements and costing procedures, contracting, or management.' Specific categories are listed as ineligible: anyone who took part in the cost study under appeal; anyone directly associated with the function in the cost study; anyone working in the activity or with household members working in the activity; anyone working for the command or organization having direct jurisdiction or control over the activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Army emphasizes impartiality and avoidance of even the appearance of conflicts; chairperson has additional stricter criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Army AAB chairperson criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The chairperson must '[b]e from an organization that neither supports or receives support from the activity in the cost study under appeal; [b]e from another installation or command or from the MACOM; [b]e of the same or higher rank or grade as the official who approved the initial decision.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stricter than Air Force standards; intended to avoid conflicts and ensure independent leadership of appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Navy 'actual appeal period' handling and information sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: OPNAVINSTR 4860.7C refers to the 20-day public review period as the 'actual appeal period' and requires the contracting officer, within 2 working days of the end of the appeal period, to provide copies of timely appeals to all 'directly affected parties.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affected parties are then given 3 working days to comment on objections and provide supporting documentation; Navy's practice of early information sharing is praised as facilitating focus on merits of disputed issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Navy AAO qualifications and team vs individual review
rubrics_metrics.description: OPNAVINSTR 4860.7C provides little guidance beyond the Supplemental Handbook and adds that if the individual is military, they must be of the same or higher rank than the individual who approved the Management Plan; it makes no mention of required specialized knowledge or expertise and appears to allow a single individual to conduct the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Less rigorous than Army or recent Air Force Interim Change; may result in less multidisciplinary review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Navy handling of errors not under appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the AAO is not 'responsible to re-audit the entire cost comparison,' if an individual discovers a procedural or computational error not the subject of an appeal, that individual is to note the error and any correction in the final appeal decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language suggests Navy is concerned about identifying and correcting all errors discovered, similar to Army practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: DoD Interim Guidance limiting AAP review to appealed items
rubrics_metrics.description: DoD Interim Guidance states '[t]he AAP Authority shall only review items specifically identified in an appeal; therefore, the AAP Authority may not make any changes to the cost comparison form unless identified in an appeal.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinforces narrow, appellant-driven scope of AAP review at the DoD level, contrasting with Army's broader practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement encouraging review by all interested parties (OMB Transmittal No. 22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transmittal Memo No. 22 and revisions to Supplemental Handbook stress that 'all interested parties, including the tentative winner of a cost comparison decision,' should submit appeals 'within the initial administrative appeal period.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy intent is to ensure all affected stakeholders examine documentation and raise errors promptly rather than sequentially.
